customer_name: Nathan S Kline Institute For Psych Res

citations.narrative:
1. The remnants of a plastic zip-tie was observed hanging from a non human primate enclosure. One end was extending
into the enclosure and had jagged edges which indicated the animal had been chewing on it. This could lead to the
possible ingestion of the material and could negatively affect the health of the animal. Enclosures and objects which NHP
come into contact with must be maintained or removed and replaced when worn in order to minimize harm to the animal
housed within. The item was removed at the time of inspection.
2. Multiple enrichment items were identified with deep grooves and jagged edges. This items were being used to hold
some of the diet/food material in accordance with the non human primate enrichment plan. This condition can affect the
ability for the item to be effectively sanitized, and can harbor bacteria and debris. Enclosures and objects which NHP
come into contact with must be maintained or removed and replaced when worn in order to minimize harm to the animal
housed within. The items were removed at the time of inspection.
******Corrected on June 1, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
